items.title: 68252_Jay Cee
items.q: George Whiting, who was a partner of mine, was one of the few names who collaborated with Irving Berlin.

ctx.x: These are the words of JC:

George Whiting, who was a partner of mine, was one of the few names who collaborated with Irving Berlin. They wrote "When My Wife's Going to the County, Hooray, Hooray" -- George Whiting thought a lot of Berlin and Berlin, thought a lot of Whiting. That was in 1905.

I dreamed of working with Whiting one day, but never dreamed it would happen -- and later, to become part of a guy who had been part of another guy, if you know what I mean? Oh my goodness, we were playing one day, "Belive it, Beloved" and Irving Berlin was there listening to it. He liked it a lot. He was singing it, singing it right out, and suddenly George says, "Come on, let's get out of here, if he can sing it, he can rewrite it!"
